verses.1: Bless my soul the LORD, the LORD my God, you have magnified so much. Splendor and majesty you have clothed yourself with.
verses.2: Covering light like a garment, stretching the heavens like a canopy.
verses.3: The one who shelters above the waters his lofty heights, the one who sets clouds as his chariot, the one who walks on the wings of wind.
verses.4: The one who makes his angels spirits, his ministers a flaming fire.
verses.5: He founded the earth on its firmaments; it will not waver forever and ever.
verses.6: The deep like a garment is its covering, on the mountains the waters will stand.
verses.7: From your rebuke they will flee, from the voice of your thunder they will be afraid.
verses.8: The mountains will rise, the valleys will descend to the place you have established for them.
verses.9: You set a boundary they will not cross, they will not return to cover the earth.
verses.10: The one who sends springs in the gullies, between the mountains the waters will flow.
verses.11: They will quench all the beasts of the field, the wild donkeys will satisfy their thirst.
verses.12: On them the birds of the heavens will dwell, from between the rocks they will give voice.
verses.13: Watering the mountains from his lofty heights, from the fruit of your works the earth will be satisfied.
verses.14: The one who causes grass to sprout for the livestock and plants for the service of humanity, to bring forth bread from the earth.
verses.15: And wine to gladden the heart of a human, to make the face shine with oil, and bread to sustain the heart of a human.
verses.16: The trees of the LORD will be satisfied, the cedars of Lebanon which he planted.
verses.17: In them the storks will nest, the coney will find a home for the rock-badger.
verses.18: The high mountains for the wild goats, the rocks a refuge for the hyraxes.
verses.19: He made the moon for seasons, the sun knows its rising.
verses.20: You set darkness and it becomes night; in it all the beasts of the forest will roam.
verses.21: The lions will roar for prey, to seek their food from God.
verses.22: The sun will rise and they will gather, and to their dens they will lie down.
verses.23: A human will go out to his work, to his labor until evening.
verses.24: How many are your works, LORD! You have made all of them with wisdom; the earth is full of your possessions.
verses.25: This the great sea, vast and wide, there crawling things innumerable, small creatures together with the great.
verses.26: There ships will go, the leviathan you made to play in it.
verses.27: All of them look to you, to give them their food in its season.
verses.28: You give to them, they will gather; you open your hand, they will be satisfied with good.
verses.29: You hide your face, they will be frightened; you take away their breath, they will perish, and return to their dust.
verses.30: You send forth your spirit, they are created; you renew the face of the earth.
verses.31: Let the glory of the LORD be forever; the LORD will rejoice in his works.
verses.32: The one who looks to the earth and it trembles, the one who touches the mountains and they smoke.
verses.33: I will sing to the LORD in my life; I will make music to my God while I still live.
verses.34: May my meditation be pleasing to him; I will rejoice in the LORD.
verses.35: Let the wicked be wiped out from the earth, and the evildoers be no more. Bless my soul the LORD. Praise the name!

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "Bless my soul the LORD" is a literal rendering of "Bar'khi nafshi et YHWH" that avoids the archaic "let my soul bless."
- v. 3: "The one who shelters" is an interpretive rendering of "ha-meqar" to reflect the divine sovereignty over the waters.
- v. 13: "Watering the mountains from his lofty heights" renders "mashekh ha-harim mi-aliyotav" as a poetic image of divine provision.
- v. 17: "The coney" is an alternative rendering of "chasidei roshim" (lit. "holy ones of the heads") as "rock-badgers" or "hyraxes."
- v. 24: "Your possessions" renders "kinyanekha" to reflect the richness of the earth as belonging to the LORD.
- v. 35: "Wipe out" renders "yitamu" to preserve the poetic contrast with the final blessing.
